newsitem.title: BELGIUM: TENNIS-HENMAN OVERCOMES CLAVET TO REACH SEMIFINALS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HENMAN OVERCOMES CLAVET TO REACH SEMIFINALS.

text.p: Britain's Tim Henman, the only seeded player to survive the second round, beat unseeded Francisco Clavet 7-6 6-4 to reach the semifinals of the European Community championhip on Friday.
Czech players had contrasting fortunes in earlier quarter-final matches with Petr Korda winning easily but Martin Damm retiring against German Marc Goellner after four games.
Sixth-seeded Henman, the world number 19, faces Goellner in his semifinal while Korda meets either Belgian lucky loser Filip Dewulf or Swiss Marc Rosset in the other half of the draw.
"It's going to be a tough match. He's full of confidence but he has to beat me. That's the best part," Goellner said of Henman.
Henman took the first-set tiebreak 7-4 and battled back from 3-0 down in the second set.
He converted his third match point when world number 34 Clavet hit a lob long.
Clavet, a natural baseliner, squandered the chance to take a 5-2 lead in the second set when he allowed Henman to recover from 40-0 down and break his service.
Korda trounced Belgian qualifier Dick Norman, the tallest player on the ATP tour at 2.03 metres, 6-3 6-4.
Damm, who had sprained his ankle in the final set of his second-round match against second-seeded Chilean Marcelo Rios on Thursday, was trailing Goellner 3-1 in the first set when he pulled out.
"I did not expect him to give up," said Goellner. "I saw him in the locker room before and he did about 10 to 15 kangaroo jumps and I thought 'okay, he's top fit'," he said.
But he soon noted that Damm, who had also played a doubles match after hurting his ankle, appeared slower and his service weaker than usual.
Norman said he felt somewhat tired mentally and physically after his late night shock win over fifth seed Felix Mantilla of Spain on Thursday.
"I just was unable to attack on Korda's service," he said.
Korda said he was not feeling 100 percent after a bout of flu before a Davis Cup tie with India two weeks ago.
Henman, who said his goal now was to break into the top 10, said Clavet had made life very difficult for him.
"Against somebody like Clavet you have to take risks because he'll obviously stay out there all day and won't miss too many balls," he said.
"I didn't want to get into a battle in his type of game."
Henman said he was still not playing to his full potential and felt he could improve all aspects of his game.
